sections.text: निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।
O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment as regards this problem. It has a threefold aspect.
Acts of sacrifice, benevolence and austerity should not be given up but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।
But they should be done with detachment and without thought of recompense. This is my final judgment.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. This is a constant theme in our discussion: that to enjoy something, you have to give up something. So all throughout Bhagavad Gita you hear these two words, Tyaga and Sannyasa.
Our normal connotation is that if I give up something, I have lost something. But Upanishads and Bhagavad Gita constantly tell us, to gain something you have to give up something. You are giving up something because you want to gain something.
When Upanishads like Isha Vasya Upanishad say Isha vasyam idam sarvam -- that this world is pervaded by that one single entity. Everything in this world, Jagatyam jagat, that which you see in this Jagat, is all pervaded by the same Ishvara, the same entity. Tena tyaktena bhunjita -- you protect that entity within you by detachment.
If you attach to something else, youll be detached from your own self. So the main theme of Bhagavad Gita is that you should give up all attachments to enjoy the bliss which youre seeking. That perennial happiness that youre seeking can only be enjoyed by giving up the attachments to the world of plurality.
So we have been discussing these two terms from chapter two onward -- Tyaga and Sannyasa. This chapter opened with Arjuna saying, I want to understand these two terms Tyaga and Sannyasa in detail so there is no confusion. What is Tyaga and what is Sannyasa? We have talked about Tyaga and Sannyasa as if theyre the same thing.
Giving up something and renouncing something. I give up my Samsara or I renounce my Samsara. But as we discussed last time, giving up coffee is Tyaga.
I will not drink coffee from tomorrow. That doesnt mean that my attachment to coffee is gone. I will have a lingering thought of coffee. Renouncing is completely detaching yourself from the thought of coffee.
So thats renunciation. So Bhagavan explains here in very simple terms: Kamyanam Karmanam Nyasah Sanyasam Kavayo Vidhu. The sages who have realized the truth in their meditation and contemplation then give out that truth in poetry.
In the richas, in Vedas they are called kavis. Those who have written poetry. These sages have said that Karmanam Nyasam it is sannyasam.
Giving up the desire prompted actions is sannyas. You dont have to give up your clothes. You dont have to shave your head.
You dont have to run away from this world. Bhagavad said the giving up Karmanam Kamya Naam. But then what is tyaga? He says Sarvakarma Farad Tyagam Prahu Tyagam Vichakshanah.
Wise people say that giving up the anxiety for the fruits of actions is tyaga. That I have given all my worries to the Karma Phala Datta. Karma Phala Datta is always somebody other than the one who is acting. I am always the actor in the present.
I act, result comes in future is always in somebody elses hand, not in mine. If something which I dont have any control over to worry about it is seems silly. But we do that all the time.
So Bhagavan said that one who has given up that anxiety of the fruits of actions is the tyagi. And then he said some people say that all actions are imperfect. There is not a perfect action in this world.
Everything will have a main result and a side effect. Something which is good will always have some imperfection in it or something not good attached to it. And something which is evil will also some good attached to it.
Climate change may be disastrous to one region. It helps other region. I was watching one of those TV channel.
Whatever that fish is migrating upward. So now there were less production in USA but more production in Canada. So what is lost for the USA is gain for the Canada.
So theres always something which is contrary to what a popularly understood the result of the action is. So Bhagavan said that some people say therefore give up all actions because they are all imperfect. They will never give you perfect results.
Your goal is to get the perfect happiness in life by working in this world. But even good actions will not give you the perfect happiness. Thats what we say in this class.
Doing good is not good enough. That still binds you to those good results. You feel good about doing something, you want to continue doing it.
Then the world doesnt let you do it and now youre mad. So some people say therefore give up all actions. But Bhagavan says no.
My opinion is you should not give up Yajna Dana Tapaha Karma -- the actions of yajna, dana, and tapa. And then we have this confusion about what Yajna, Dana, and Tapa are for. Im doing it for others, Im sacrificing, Im giving to somebody else, Im doing charity for others.
So this verse clarifies that for you. Nischayam Srunume Tatra Tyagay Bharatar Sabha, Tyagohi Purusha Vyagraha Trivedha Sampra Kirti Tah. Listen to me conclusively what Tyaga is.
Tyagahi Trividha Sampra Kirti Tah. Tyaga is also of three types. Two things are very common in our discussion in Bhagavad Gita. One is Tyaga and Renunciation.
Second is Trigunas, satv, Rajas and Tamas. So Bhagawan said, let me tell you conclusively what Tyaga is. And also you should know that Tyaga is also of three types of it can be classified in the same way we have classified Ahara Yagna Tapa.
All this in previous chapter Tag also can be classified in three. And Bhagavan addresses Arjuna as Purusha Vyagara, a tiger among men, boosting his morale that you can do it. Yajna Dana Tapaha Karman Karyam Eva Tat, Yagna Dana Tapahachayeva Pavanani Manishina.
Here comes why Dana is for you and not for others. He said Yajna, Dana, and Tapa Karma should not be given up, because Yajna, Dana, and Tapa are the purifiers even for the wise. But actually there is no word even in the Sanskrit here; it simply says for the wise people. Also, continuing education -- in any profession that we are in, unless you continue your education, you get stale.
So when I was going for my eye surgery, when I subluxated eye lens, my cataract done four years ago, my lens has moved out. Its actually 90 degree. So obviously I didnt feel anything.
But everybody who told me what it is pretty scary situation. So I told my first surgeon that I think I want to go with somebody who has a lot of experience, who looks like me with gray hair. He said, no, no, no, Rajan, dont do that.
Because they are all stale, their knowledge is all outdated, you know, to go with somebody whos fresh, who has the latest knowledge. So I go to the next guy and ask him how many years of experience? How many surgeries you have done? I said, Ill go with the stale guy, the guy whose knowledge is 10 years old. So I went with a guy who said I do it routinely for everybody, like six surgery in a month like this.
So we also can say that a wise person can veer off from his knowledge. He has to constantly be on his toes to keep his mind pure. So he said this will only help wise people who are constantly doing this to keep their knowledge pristine.
If youre doing yajnadanand tapa and you have no intention of getting any benefit out of it for you, then obviously its not going to be of any value. But it will help people who are wise enough to know the value of this. That keeping my mind and intellect pure, I need to constantly be working on it because there are lots of temptations out there in this world.
And when I slip from my wisdom, nobody will know. Therefore I have to be constantly vigilant about keeping my mind and intellect -- which is my internal instrument -- pure, so that the knowledge can shine through. So therefore he says, yajna dana tapaacha pavanani manishinam.
So wise people, they constantly do yajna dana and tapa to keep their internal instrument pure. So he said, this is for you to keep yourself pure so that the knowledge will always be with you. Etan apitu karmani sangam tyaktva falanicha kartabyan ITI me partha nischitam matam uttamam.
And now he says that Im going to give you my final opinion. This is my best and final opinion. So there is no confusion.
So up till now Bhagavan said, Im not the first one to tell you. Many sages have come and told you that. Now Im telling you same knowledge.
Here he comes and tells Arjuna, this is my best and final opinion for you. Because he realized that Arjuna is probably at a point where he will listen to me more than Vedas and Upanishads. He said, Im telling you itana pito carmani sangam tyaktva falanicha.
Even these actions of yajna danan tapa should be done with sangam tyaktva by giving up attachment and falanicha and giving up fruits. So two things we constantly hear, you have to detach and you have to give up. Detach from that which is not real, that which is of not any use.
So there are now lots of seminars on how to keep your house healthy and happy. And their claim is to give up everything which you dont use. Take out everything from your house which you have not used in last three years, last five years, keep it out and keep what you really need.
And that will make you happy. So Bhagavan said, sangam tyaktva, detach from things which are of no value to you in this world. The objects which cannot give you happiness.
Be detached from that and fala nature and also detached from the expectations for the fruit. Because even doing good, when I have an expectation of something good coming out of, ties me to the anxiety. The Bhagavan said, yajna dana and tapa should be done for one simple reason.
To purify your mind and intellect, your internal instrument. Because thats all you as a seeker has to do. Rest of it Bhagavan has to do.
Its like all you have to do is eat digestion. I dont have to worry about it. He needs to take care of it.
Same way Bhagavan said, all you have to do is keep your mind and intellect pure. Ill take care of it. So therefore its a you do not worry about your actions.
Give up the attachment to your actions. Whether I could do it or not, did I do it right or not? Lets not get attached to it. Do for purifying your mind and intellect without any attachment and any expectations from your actions.
Even expectation this will purify my mind can become a burden. You do for your simple motive of finding that ultimate happiness. Bhagawan says, rest, I will take care of it.
Therefore he says, karthiya Bhyanidi, do all these actions as I prescribed. Partha nischitam matam uttam. This is my best and final opinion.
Do actions which are purifying your mind. And that means which we consider the punya Karma. Papa, Karma are the ones which are giving negative impressions on our mind.
They should be avoided anywhere. But the ones which I am doing it to earn punya even they should be done without attachment, without an expectation for the fruits. Bhagawan says thats my best and final opinion.
We had been discussing chapter 18, Moksa Sanyasa Yoga. We have seen the conclusion of Bhagavad Gita. The last verse we had discussed is said Sarva Dharman parityajya Mamekam Sharanam Braja Ahamtwa Sarva Pape bhy moksha Shyamima Sucha.
Thats the conclusion. Thats the essence of the entire Bhagavad Gita.

Krishna delivers his best and final opinion in these verses: yajna (sacrifice), dana (charity), and tapa (austerity) should never be abandoned because they are pavanani manishinam - purifiers even for the wise. This is a revolutionary teaching. We might think that highly evolved souls no longer need spiritual practices, but Krishna insists that even wise people require continuous purification of their internal instruments. It is like continuing education for any profession - without it, even experts become stale. The practices of sacrifice, giving, and discipline are not just for beginners; they are lifetime companions on the spiritual journey.
The profound insight here is that yajna, dana, and tapa are ultimately for you, not for others. When you give charity, the primary beneficiary is your own mind and heart being purified. When you practice austerity, your internal instrument becomes clearer. Krishnas instruction is precise: perform these actions sangam tyaktva phalani cha - without attachment and without expectation of results. Even the expectation that this practice will purify my mind can become a subtle burden.
Reflect today: What is your relationship with your spiritual practices? Do you perform them with a scorekeepers mentality, tracking progress and expecting results? Or can you engage in service, giving, and discipline simply because they need to be done? Try this exercise: Perform one act of generosity today with absolutely no expectation - not even the expectation of feeling good about it. Give anonymously if possible, and observe what happens in your inner world when no one knows and no result is anticipated.
